laws.title: Sri Lankan Culture — Head Wobble and Temple Respect
laws.subtitle: The head wobble means yes; remove shoes at temples
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's distinctive 'head wobble' (side-to-side head movement) is a positive response meaning yes, okay, or I understand — don't confuse with 'no'. Temple visits: dress modestly, remove shoes, remain quiet. Buddhism is practiced by ~70% of the population — treat monks with great respect, never hand objects directly to monks (place on a table instead). The greeting is 'Ayubowan' with palms pressed together.
laws.penalty: Disrespecting Buddhist monks or temples: possible arrest. Destroying Buddhist property: criminal offence.
exceptions: Hindu Tamil communities have different customs in the north
Urban Colombo is more cosmopolitan

quiz.q: What does the 'head wobble' mean in Sri Lanka?
quiz.explanation: The Sri Lankan head wobble (side-to-side) is a positive gesture meaning yes, okay, or I understand — the opposite of what many Westerners expect.

laws.title: Buddha Statue Selfie Law — Turning Back to Buddha is Criminal
laws.subtitle: Bhikku Act and Buddhist Temporalities — Disrespecting Buddhism
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka has specific laws protecting Buddhist religious sentiments. Posing with your back to a Buddha statue for a selfie or photograph is considered disrespectful and tourists have been deported or arrested for it. In 2012, three French tourists were arrested for posing 'disrespectfully' with Buddha images. In 2014, a UK tourist was deported for a Buddha tattoo deemed disrespectful. The law is actively enforced at religious sites.
laws.penalty: Insulting Buddhist religion: up to 2 years imprisonment + deportation for foreigners. Incidents reviewed case-by-case.
exceptions: Respectful photography facing the statue is generally fine
Academic and documentary photography with permission
laws.sourceLabel: Sri Lanka Immigration and Tourism Authority

quiz.q: What happened to tourists who posed with their backs to Buddha statues in Sri Lanka?
quiz.explanation: Several tourists have been arrested, fined, or deported from Sri Lanka for posing disrespectfully with Buddha statues — including for Buddha tattoos.

laws.title: LGBTQ+ Laws — Criminal; Possible Imprisonment
laws.subtitle: Penal Code §365 and §365A — Up to 10 years
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka criminalises same-sex relations under Penal Code sections 365 and 365A, with penalties of up to 10 years imprisonment. Despite being a relatively liberal tourist destination for South Asia, same-sex relations remain illegal. LGBTQ+ activists have been arrested at events. Discrimination is widespread. Reform efforts have been proposed but not enacted.
laws.penalty: Same-sex relations: up to 10 years imprisonment. Gross indecency: up to 2 years.
exceptions: No formal enforcement exceptions
Private conduct is less likely to be prosecuted but not protected

quiz.q: Sri Lanka's Penal Code carries a maximum penalty for same-sex relations of?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Penal Code §365 and §365A carry up to 10 years imprisonment for same-sex relations — though prosecutions are less frequent than discrimination and harassment.

laws.title: Traffic Laws — Left-Side Driving; Strict Seatbelt Law
laws.subtitle: Motor Traffic Act — Left side; 0.08% BAC limit
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka drives on the left (British legacy). The drink driving limit is 0.08% BAC. Seatbelts are mandatory for all occupants. Helmets mandatory for motorcyclists. Speed limits: 50km/h urban, 70km/h rural. Mobile phone use while driving is prohibited. Tuk-tuks (three-wheelers) are the most popular tourist transport — insist on the meter or negotiate before starting. Colombo traffic is heavy; Sri Lankan drivers often use horns heavily (culturally normal, not aggressive).
laws.penalty: Drink driving above 0.08%: fine LKR 25,000 + licence suspension. No helmet: fine LKR 2,500. Mobile phone: fine LKR 2,500.
exceptions: None for drink driving limit

quiz.q: What is the most popular tourist transport in Sri Lanka, typically requiring meter or pre-negotiation?
quiz.explanation: Tuk-tuks (three-wheelers / auto-rickshaws) are the most popular tourist transport in Sri Lanka — always insist on using the meter or negotiate the price before getting in.

laws.title: Drug Laws — 6 Year Mandatory Minimum; Death for Large Quantities
laws.subtitle: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance — No. 17 of 1929 (amended)
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka has very strict drug laws. Drug trafficking above threshold quantities can result in the death penalty. Possession of any controlled substance (cannabis, heroin, cocaine) results in mandatory imprisonment. Courts must sentence to at least 6 years for certain quantities. Cannabis plants are found growing wild in some rural areas — possession of even naturally found cannabis is illegal. Enforcement is active at the airport and in tourist areas like Arugam Bay and Hikkaduwa.
laws.penalty: Trafficking large quantities: death penalty possible. Possession: 6 years mandatory minimum. Small possession: 2–5 years. Using: treatment or imprisonment.
exceptions: Ayurvedic medicines using licensed herbal compounds under Department of Ayurveda
No practical tolerance for recreational cannabis even in areas where it grows wild
laws.sourceLabel: Poisons Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance — Sri Lanka

quiz.q: What is the mandatory minimum sentence for drug possession above threshold amounts in Sri Lanka?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's drug laws impose a mandatory minimum of 6 years imprisonment for certain drug quantities — and large trafficking amounts can attract the death penalty.

laws.title: Photography Restrictions — Military Sites and Government Buildings
laws.subtitle: Prevention of Terrorism Act & National Security Rules — camera restrictions near sensitive sites
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka, still recovering from a 26-year civil war that ended in 2009, maintains strict rules around photographing military installations, army checkpoints, government buildings, and certain strategic infrastructure. The Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) — widely criticised by human rights groups — has been used to detain people including tourists who photographed checkpoints or military parades. Photographing military personnel without permission is discouraged and can lead to questioning or detention. Additional sensitivity exists around photographs that could be construed as showing military positions. The rules are not always clearly posted, making unintentional violations possible.
laws.penalty: Photographing prohibited military or government installations: detention for questioning; serious cases under PTA: up to 18 months preventive detention without trial.
exceptions: Clearly designated tourist viewpoints near historical fortifications (e.g. Galle Fort, Sigiriya)
Organised media with accreditation and specific permissions
laws.sourceLabel: Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) — Parliament of Sri Lanka

quiz.q: Why are photography restrictions especially strict in Sri Lanka near military sites?
options: Sensitivity following the 26-year civil war that ended in 2009
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's civil war ended in 2009 after 26 years, and post-war security remains sensitive — the Prevention of Terrorism Act has been used to detain people who photographed military checkpoints or installations.

laws.title: Kandy Temple of the Tooth — Strict Dress Code; Buddha Tattoos Face Entry Ban
laws.subtitle: Dalada Maligawa — Sacred relic; tattoo and dress rules strictly enforced
laws.fullDescription: The Temple of the Tooth Relic (Sri Dalada Maligawa) in Kandy is Sri Lanka's most sacred Buddhist site, housing a tooth relic of the Buddha. Entry rules are strictly enforced: all visitors must remove shoes and hats, wear clothing covering shoulders and knees (sarong wraps are provided at the entrance), and turn off phone ringtones. Drums and traditional music (Kandyan drummers) accompany the three daily puja (offerings) — photography during puja is restricted. Buddha tattoos became controversial in 2012 when a British tourist was deported for having Buddha tattoos on her arm — Sri Lanka officially bans entry for anyone displaying Buddha images tattooed on their body under religious protection law.
laws.penalty: Entering temple with Buddha tattoos visible: deportation under Section 290 of the Penal Code (insult to religion). Improper dress at temple: refusal of entry.
exceptions: Academic Buddhist scholars with invitations from the temple authority
Diplomatic guests at official ceremonies
laws.sourceLabel: Sri Dalada Maligawa — Temple of the Tooth Relic

quiz.q: What happened to a British tourist in Sri Lanka in 2012 who had a Buddha tattoo on her arm?
options: She was asked to cover the tattoo
She was briefly detained then released
quiz.explanation: In 2012, a British tourist was deported from Sri Lanka for having a Buddha tattoo on her arm — considered an insult to Buddhism under Sri Lankan law. Sri Lanka has deported several tourists for Buddha-related tattoos.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Elephant Protection — Wild Elephants Cannot Be Owned Without Heritage Status
laws.subtitle: Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance — Wild elephants: strictly protected
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka has approximately 6,000–7,000 wild Asian elephants — the highest density of wild elephants in Asia. The Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance strictly prohibits capturing, keeping, or selling wild elephants. The 'night safaris' in some private areas where tourists get very close to elephants in vehicles are regulated — maintaining distance from wild elephants is mandatory. Sri Lanka is also famous for domesticated temple elephants (used in Perahera festivals) — these are registered with the Department of Wildlife Conservation and cannot be bought or sold without government approval. Mistreatment of captive elephants is a criminal offence. Visitors should be cautious about paying for elephant rides — many facilities have poor welfare standards.
laws.penalty: Capturing or keeping wild elephant without authorisation: up to 5 years imprisonment + SLR 500,000. Mistreating a captive elephant: criminal charge.
exceptions: Registered captive temple elephants with Department of Wildlife Conservation permits
Research institutions with DWLC permits for non-invasive study
laws.sourceLabel: Sri Lanka Department of Wildlife Conservation

quiz.q: Approximately how many wild Asian elephants does Sri Lanka have, giving it the highest density in Asia?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka has approximately 6,000–7,000 wild Asian elephants — the highest density of wild elephants in Asia relative to land area, making elephant conservation a critical national priority.

laws.title: Aragalaya Protest Legacy — Economic Crisis Laws and Emergency Powers Record
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse and mass protests led to unprecedented presidential removal
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis — caused by forex reserve collapse, fuel shortages, and food insecurity — triggered unprecedented mass protests (the Aragalaya, meaning 'struggle'). President Gotabaya Rajapaksa declared a state of emergency multiple times, deploying military against protesters. Despite emergency powers, protesters stormed and occupied the Presidential Palace in July 2022. Rajapaksa became the first sitting Sri Lankan president to resign and flee the country. The government subsequently arrested protest leaders under the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) — a colonial-era law allowing 18-month detention without charge. IMF bailout conditions included fiscal reforms that caused further hardship. The Aragalaya demonstrated that economic grievance can override emergency powers, but also that PTA was weaponized post-protest.
laws.penalty: Under PTA: detention up to 18 months without charge. Emergency regulations: up to 5 years imprisonment for participating in prohibited gatherings. Post-protest: leaders charged with incitement and terrorism offenses.
exceptions: IMF program monitoring creates some constraints on arbitrary detention
Diplomatic intervention has secured release of some detained protesters
Lawyers challenging PTA detention have constitutional remedies through the Supreme Court
laws.sourceLabel: Amnesty International — Sri Lanka Aragalaya and PTA Report 2022-23

quiz.q: What unprecedented event occurred in July 2022 during Sri Lanka's Aragalaya protests?
options: The military staged a coup and removed the president
Protesters stormed and occupied the Presidential Palace, leading to the president's resignation
The Supreme Court dissolved parliament over economic mismanagement
The IMF sent peacekeepers to ensure its bailout conditions were met
quiz.explanation: In July 2022, protesters stormed and occupied Sri Lanka's Presidential Palace, swimming in the pool and lounging in the president's residence — within days, President Gotabaya Rajapaksa became the first sitting Sri Lankan president to resign and flee the country, boarding a military jet to the Maldives.

laws.title: Elephant Conservation vs. Human-Elephant Conflict — Sri Lanka's Escalating Crisis
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka has the highest human-elephant conflict death rate globally; laws protect elephants but tensions rise
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka has the world's highest density of Asian elephants (estimated 5,000–7,000, plus wild elephants) relative to human population — and one of the world's worst human-elephant conflict situations. The Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance (FFPO) fully protects elephants: killing, capturing, or harassing elephants is illegal. Yet approximately 70+ elephants and 70–80 people die annually in conflicts. Elephants raid crops — farmers retaliate. Elektrisk fences create their own problems (animals learn to bypass them; electrocution deaths). The Department of Wildlife Conservation (DWC) translocates 'problem elephants' to national parks but these parks are at carrying capacity. The 'Human-Elephant Coexistence' policy tries to create buffer zones. High-voltage 'kangani' fences have been blamed for elephant deaths.
laws.penalty: Killing an elephant: up to 7 years imprisonment + fines up to LKR 500,000 (~$1,600). Capturing wild elephants without permit: same penalties. Ritual elephant abuse (in perahera ceremonies): FFPO enforcement.
exceptions: DWC-authorized capture for elephant orphanages (injured/orphaned calves)
Emergency electrocution of charging elephants in genuine self-defense (contested legally)
Temple elephants registered before FFPO amendments have grandfathered status
laws.sourceLabel: Sri Lanka Department of Wildlife Conservation — Elephant Conservation

quiz.q: Approximately how many Asian elephants live in Sri Lanka, giving it one of the world's highest elephant densities?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka has an estimated 5,000–7,000 Asian elephants, making it one of the highest-density elephant countries in Asia relative to land area. This density, combined with expanding human settlements and agriculture, creates the world's highest rate of human-elephant conflict deaths per square kilometer of elephant habitat.

laws.title: 2022 Economic Collapse & Aragalaya
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's worst economic crisis led to storming of presidential palace
laws.fullDescription: In 2022, Sri Lanka experienced its worst economic crisis since independence: foreign reserves were depleted, fuel ran out, 13-hour daily power cuts hit, medicine shortages arose, and inflation exceeded 70%. The crisis was driven by pandemic-related tourism collapse, debt overhang from Chinese-financed infrastructure (including Hambantota Port), and a sudden ban on agrochemical imports that devastated rice harvests. The Aragalaya ('struggle') protest movement saw citizens occupy the presidential residence. President Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled to the Maldives and resigned. Sri Lanka reached a $2.9 billion IMF bailout agreement in 2023.
laws.penalty: State of emergency imposed July 2022. Essential services disruption laws used against protesters. Certain protest leaders detained. IMF conditions require painful austerity — tax increases and subsidy cuts.
exceptions: IMF program provides debt restructuring framework for creditors
China agreed to bilateral debt restructuring in 2023
Electricity tariff increases and fuel subsidies cuts are conditions of the bailout

quiz.q: What dramatic event marked the peak of Sri Lanka's 2022 Aragalaya protests?
options: The president fled after citizens occupied the presidential residence
quiz.explanation: At the height of Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis, protesters stormed and occupied the presidential residence, forcing President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee to the Maldives and resign.

laws.title: AKD Election Win — Left Shift After IMF Crisis
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka elected a Marxist-aligned president in 2024 amid continued IMF austerity
laws.fullDescription: In September 2024, Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) of the National People's Power (NPP/JVP) coalition won Sri Lanka's presidential election — the first victory for a left-wing party since independence. AKD's party had historically advocated against IMF programs but, once elected, committed to continuing Sri Lanka's $2.9 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility while renegotiating specific conditions. He dissolved parliament immediately and won a parliamentary supermajority in November 2024 — the first single-party majority in decades. The election reflected ongoing public anger over the 2022 economic collapse and desire for anti-corruption governance.
laws.penalty: Sri Lanka's election laws: vote buying carries fines and disqualification. Campaign finance violations: Electoral Commission sanctions. The JVP's violent past (1971 and 1987 uprisings) does not affect current legal standing.
exceptions: IMF program continues regardless of government — conditionality is binding
Debt restructuring agreed with China and bilateral creditors remains in force
The new parliamentary supermajority enables constitutional changes — requiring 2/3 majority
laws.sourceLabel: Office of the President of Sri Lanka

quiz.q: What politically unusual step did newly elected Sri Lankan President AKD take immediately after his 2024 election victory?
options: Dissolved parliament to seek a fresh mandate
quiz.explanation: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake dissolved parliament immediately after winning the September 2024 presidential election — a calculated move that succeeded in winning his NPP coalition an unprecedented parliamentary supermajority in November 2024.

laws.title: Tamil Reconciliation & War Crimes Accountability
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's civil war ended in 2009 with alleged war crimes — accountability remains elusive 15 years later
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 26-year civil war ended in May 2009 when government forces defeated the Tamil Tiger (LTTE) separatists. The final offensive killed an estimated 40,000–70,000+ Tamil civilians; the UN Panel of Experts found credible evidence of war crimes by both sides. Sri Lanka has created multiple transitional justice mechanisms (OMP — Office on Missing Persons, ONUR — reconciliation office, and a promised Truth Commission) but no criminal accountability for alleged war crimes. Tamil families of the disappeared number in the tens of thousands. The UN Human Rights Council has repeatedly called for international accountability; Sri Lanka's government opposes external involvement.
laws.penalty: No war crimes prosecutions have occurred in Sri Lanka. The OMP can investigate disappearances but cannot prosecute. Domestic courts have not pursued senior military commanders.
exceptions: The Special Court proposed in 2015 UNHRC resolution was never established
Diaspora Tamils can submit testimonies from abroad
Former combatants who surrendered were processed through reintegration programs

quiz.q: Approximately how many Tamil civilians were estimated to have been killed in the final offensive of Sri Lanka's civil war in 2009?
quiz.explanation: The UN Panel of Experts estimated 40,000–70,000+ Tamil civilians were killed in the final months of Sri Lanka's civil war in 2009 — finding credible evidence of war crimes by both government forces and the LTTE, though no criminal accountability has followed.

laws.title: Prevention of Terrorism Act & Easter Sunday Bombing Accountability
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's colonial-era terrorism law has been used to detain Muslim suspects for years without trial after the 2019 Easter attacks
laws.fullDescription: On April 21, 2019 (Easter Sunday), coordinated suicide bombings at churches and luxury hotels in Sri Lanka killed 269 people. The Islamic State claimed responsibility; the attacks were carried out by a local jihadist group. In the aftermath, Sri Lanka invoked the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) — a draconian 1979 law allowing detention without charge for up to 18 months and admitting confessions obtained under duress. Hundreds of Muslims were detained under the PTA, with many held for years without trial. Sri Lanka promised the EU and human rights bodies it would repeal or reform the PTA — the Anti-Terrorism Act was passed in 2024 but critics say it retains many of the PTA's abuses.
laws.penalty: PTA/ATA: up to 18 months detention without charge. Terrorism: death penalty (under moratorium since 1976) or 20+ years imprisonment
exceptions: The 2024 Anti-Terrorism Act created some new oversight mechanisms — a Review Board and judicial oversight — but critics say the definition of terrorism remains overbroad
Emergency regulations provide additional detention powers beyond even the ATA
laws.sourceLabel: International Commission of Jurists – Sri Lanka ATA

quiz.q: How many people were killed in Sri Lanka's 2019 Easter Sunday bombings?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2019 Easter Sunday coordinated bombings at churches and luxury hotels killed 269 people, in one of the worst terrorist attacks in South Asian history since the end of the Sri Lankan civil war.

laws.title: Aragalaya: The Protest Movement That Toppled a Dynasty
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse and 'struggle' (Aragalaya) protests forced President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee — and ended the Rajapaksa political dynasty
laws.fullDescription: In 2022, Sri Lanka experienced its worst economic crisis since independence: foreign reserves ran out, petrol queues stretched for days, power cuts lasted 13 hours daily, and medicine shortages became critical. The crisis was caused by a combination of COVID-19 tourism collapse, organic farming mandates that destroyed agricultural output, and years of tax cuts and debt accumulation under the Rajapaksa government. The 'Aragalaya' (Sinhala for 'struggle') saw hundreds of thousands occupy Galle Face Green outside the Presidential Secretariat for months. On July 9, 2022, protesters stormed and occupied the Presidential Palace; President Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled to Singapore and resigned by email. Sri Lanka negotiated a $2.9 billion IMF bailout and restructured $30+ billion in debt.
laws.penalty: Protest participants faced arrests under the Prevention of Terrorism Act. Some protesters who occupied the palace faced trespass charges, though most were released
exceptions: Aragalaya leaders negotiated partial immunity from prosecution as part of the political settlement
President Wickremesinghe (who succeeded Gotabaya) pursued IMF reform conditions rather than protest prosecutions

quiz.q: What unusual method did Sri Lankan President Gotabaya Rajapaksa use to resign after fleeing the country in 2022?
options: He sent his resignation letter by email from Singapore
He sent a text message through his secretary
His resignation was announced by the parliament speaker on his behalf
quiz.explanation: After fleeing Sri Lanka by plane to the Maldives and then Singapore following the storming of the presidential palace, Gotabaya Rajapaksa submitted his resignation by email on July 14, 2022 — an ignominious end to his presidency and the Rajapaksa political dynasty.

laws.title: Easter Bombing Prevention Law
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism Act amended after 2019 church bombings
laws.fullDescription: The 2019 Easter Sunday bombings in Sri Lanka — coordinated attacks on churches and hotels that killed 269 people — triggered amendments to the Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA) and new national security legislation. The bombings were carried out by a domestic Islamist group (National Thowheed Jamath) with suspected ISIS links. The PTA, originally enacted during the Tamil civil war (1979), was already criticized for enabling arbitrary detention and torture of Tamil suspects. Post-2019 amendments expanded the definition of terrorism and mandatory detention periods. Human rights organizations including Amnesty International documented continued abuses under the PTA against both Muslims and Tamils.
laws.penalty: Under PTA: detention without charge for up to 18 months; terrorism offenses: up to 20 years imprisonment
exceptions: PTA detainees must be brought before a magistrate within 72 hours (in theory)
Human rights organizations continue to document violations of these procedural requirements

quiz.q: How many people were killed in Sri Lanka's Easter Sunday bombings of 2019?
quiz.explanation: The Easter Sunday bombings in Sri Lanka on April 21, 2019 killed 269 people in coordinated attacks on three churches (during Easter services) and three luxury hotels, carried out by local Islamist group National Thowheed Jamath.

laws.title: Economic Crisis Emergency Laws
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse triggered emergency rule and IMF conditions
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis — caused by foreign exchange depletion, pandemic impacts, and populist tax cuts — led to fuel shortages, 13-hour power cuts, and food insecurity. President Gotabaya Rajapaksa declared a State of Emergency under the Public Security Ordinance, allowing for military rule and suppression of protests. Mass protests forced him to flee the country (July 2022) in an unprecedented people's movement. Parliament elected Ranil Wickremesinghe as president. Sri Lanka's IMF bailout (2023) required severe austerity: tax increases, utility price hikes, and state enterprise restructuring. Emergency laws were repeatedly renewed during the restructuring period.
laws.penalty: Violations of emergency regulations during the 2022 crisis: arrest without warrant, detention without trial for up to 18 months
exceptions: Civil society and protest rights were theoretically maintained under the constitution even during emergency
International journalists retained access (though some were detained temporarily)

quiz.q: What forced Sri Lanka's President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee the country in 2022?
options: A constitutional vote of no confidence
Mass popular protests storming the presidential palace
quiz.explanation: Hundreds of thousands of Sri Lankans, furious over the economic collapse causing fuel shortages and power cuts, stormed the presidential palace in July 2022. Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled to the Maldives and then Singapore, eventually resigning from abroad.

laws.title: Online Safety Act 2023
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's sweeping online content law raises free speech concerns
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act (No. 9 of 2023) was enacted in January 2024 amid significant controversy. The law establishes an Online Safety Commission with powers to issue takedown orders for 'prohibited statements' — broadly defined to include statements that threaten national security, public order, racial or religious harmony, or are deemed 'false.' The Commission can order internet service providers and social media platforms to remove content within 24 hours. Critics including the Bar Association of Sri Lanka, civil society groups, and international press freedom organizations argued the law's vague definitions could be used to suppress political dissent and legitimate journalism, especially given Sri Lanka's history of cracking down on critics during and after the civil war. The law was passed amid the country's recovery from the 2022 economic crisis that saw mass protests topple President Gotabaya Rajapaksa.
laws.penalty: Hosting prohibited statements: up to 5 years imprisonment and/or fine of 1 million Sri Lankan rupees; platforms face fines of up to 5 million rupees for non-compliance
exceptions: Content shared for educational or research purposes with proper context
Official government communications
Archived news content with appropriate labeling

laws.title: Economic Crisis, IMF Program, and Debt Restructuring
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's 2022 bankruptcy led to the first IMF program for a defaulting South Asian country
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka declared itself bankrupt in April 2022 — the first time in its independent history — after foreign exchange reserves fell below $50 million (barely enough for one week of imports), fuel and medicine became unavailable, and the economy collapsed following years of unsustainable debt accumulation, tax cuts, and the COVID-19 tourism collapse. President Gotabaya Rajapaksa fled after mass protests and resigned. In March 2023, Sri Lanka reached a $2.9 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility agreement, which required significant legal changes: tax increases (VAT raised from 8% to 18%); state enterprise reform; restructuring of sovereign bonds (a $12.5 billion external debt restructuring was completed in 2024); and anti-corruption measures. The Sri Lanka Electricity Amendment Act and Ceylon Petroleum Corporation reforms addressed state enterprise losses. Sri Lanka's debt-to-GDP ratio exceeded 100% at the peak of the crisis.
laws.penalty: IMF program non-compliance results in fund disbursement suspension; domestic anti-corruption measures include criminal prosecution of officials responsible for financial mismanagement; bond default consequences include credit rating impacts
exceptions: Concessional loans from multilateral development banks had preferential restructuring terms
Domestic pension funds were partially protected from debt restructuring
Essential public services maintained spending floors under IMF agreement

laws.title: 2024 Presidential Election and Anti-Corruption Wave
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's 2024 election brought the JVP/NPP to power for first time on an anti-corruption platform
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election produced a historic result: Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP)/National People's Power (NPP) alliance won with approximately 42% of votes in a first-past-the-post presidential election, defeating the establishment candidate Sajith Premadasa. The JVP had previously been associated with two armed insurgencies (1971 and 1987-89). The NPP's anti-corruption, anti-establishment platform resonated with voters traumatized by the 2022 economic crisis. Parliamentary elections in November 2024 gave the NPP a two-thirds majority — allowing constitutional amendments. Sri Lanka's constitution (1978) has been heavily amended but retains a powerful executive presidency, which AKD occupied. The election represented a complete sweep of traditional political families (Rajapaksa, Bandaranaike, Wickremesinghe) that had dominated Sri Lankan politics for 70+ years. The new government continued IMF program compliance while promising to renegotiate some conditions.
laws.penalty: Sri Lanka's election laws: voter fraud criminal prosecution; campaign finance violations: Election Commission enforcement
exceptions: Incumbent president has constitutionally protected term completion if not removed
Diaspora Sri Lankans cannot vote in presidential elections
Proportional representation applies to parliamentary but not presidential elections

laws.title: IMF Bailout and Economic Recovery After 2022 Crisis
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka secured a $2.9 billion IMF program after defaulting on foreign debt
laws.fullDescription: Following Sri Lanka's catastrophic 2022 economic collapse — the worst since independence, featuring empty fuel stations, medicine shortages, and the storming of President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's residence by protesters — the country secured a $2.9 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility in March 2023. The bailout required painful austerity measures: raising taxes, cutting fuel subsidies, and restructuring debt. Sri Lanka suspended debt payments to external creditors. By 2024, under President Ranil Wickremesinghe, debt restructuring agreements were reached with bilateral creditors (India, Japan, China, Paris Club) and a bond exchange was agreed with private creditors. The new president Anura Kumara Dissanayake (elected September 2024) pledged to maintain IMF commitments while reducing austerity.
laws.penalty: Failure to comply with IMF-conditioned revenue measures: program suspension and loss of disbursements. Tax evasion under reformed regime: enhanced penalties under new Inland Revenue Act.
exceptions: Debt service suspended during restructuring period under standstill agreements
Humanitarian imports exempt from most import restrictions

quiz.q: What economic milestone did Sri Lanka reach in 2022 that precipitated the IMF bailout?
options: A default on foreign debt — the country's first since independence
GDP falling by more than 50% in a single year
The currency losing 99% of its value
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka defaulted on its foreign debt in 2022 — the first sovereign default in its post-independence history — triggering the economic collapse, mass protests, and eventual IMF bailout program.

laws.title: Sri Lanka's Tax Reform and Revenue Mobilization Under IMF
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka raised taxes dramatically as a condition of its IMF bailout program
laws.fullDescription: As part of Sri Lanka's $2.9 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility (2023), the country committed to significantly increasing tax revenue — which had fallen to around 8% of GDP (among the world's lowest). The IMF required Sri Lanka to raise this to 15% by 2025. Tax reforms included: raising VAT from 12% to 18%, introducing a new Social Security Contribution Levy, lowering income tax thresholds, and tightening corporate tax avoidance. President Ranil Wickremesinghe faced public anger over tax rises during a cost-of-living crisis. The elected president Anura Kumara Dissanayake (September 2024) pledged to maintain IMF commitments while reviewing specific tax measures. Sri Lanka's debt restructuring with bilateral and private creditors continued through 2024-2025.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion under Inland Revenue Act: fines up to 3x evaded amount plus imprisonment. VAT fraud: up to 5 years and 3x fine.
exceptions: Essential food items (rice, bread, fish) exempt from VAT
Exports zero-rated for VAT
Small businesses below revenue threshold subject to simplified tax regime
laws.sourceLabel: Inland Revenue Department of Sri Lanka

quiz.q: What did Sri Lanka's IMF bailout require regarding tax revenue as a share of GDP?
options: Raising tax revenue from approximately 8% of GDP to 15% by 2025
Reducing taxes to attract foreign investment while cutting spending
Introducing a 5% wealth tax on all assets above $1 million
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's IMF program required raising tax revenue from approximately 8% of GDP (among the world's lowest) to 15% by 2025 — necessitating dramatic tax increases during an ongoing cost-of-living crisis, including raising VAT from 12% to 18%.

laws.title: Sri Lanka's Economic Crisis Emergency Laws
laws.subtitle: 2022 economic collapse led to state of emergency and emergency economic powers
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis — the worst since independence — resulted from foreign exchange shortages, food and fuel scarcity, and unsustainable debt. President Gotabaya Rajapaksa declared multiple states of emergency granting security forces expanded powers. After his resignation following mass protests, the government enacted the Economic Transformation Act providing the IMF-required framework for fiscal consolidation, state-owned enterprise reform, and debt restructuring. Essential services workers are prohibited from striking under emergency provisions.
laws.penalty: Violating emergency curfews: up to 1 year imprisonment. Strikes in essential services during emergency: up to 2 years. Spreading 'false news' during emergency: up to 2 years. Protests near parliament and Presidential Secretariat: restricted zones with immediate arrest powers
exceptions: IMF debt restructuring negotiations required exemptions from some constitutional budget rules
Foreign creditors have separate negotiated restructuring terms
Pharmaceutical imports had emergency expedited clearance exemptions

quiz.q: What triggered Sri Lanka's declaration of multiple states of emergency in 2022?
options: A severe economic crisis with fuel and food shortages
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis — caused by foreign exchange shortages leading to fuel, food, and medicine scarcity — prompted the government to declare multiple states of emergency, eventually leading to President Rajapaksa's resignation.

laws.title: Sri Lanka's Dissanayake Election and IMF Reforms
laws.subtitle: Marxist-leaning president wins on anti-corruption platform amid recovery
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election was won by Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) / National People's Power alliance — a leftist politician who campaigned against corruption and IMF austerity measures, then won and continued the IMF program anyway. AKD's party then won parliamentary elections in November 2024 with a two-thirds majority. Sri Lanka continued its IMF Extended Fund Facility program, implementing painful fiscal consolidation including new taxes and pension reforms. The Domestic Debt Optimization completed debt restructuring with domestic creditors. External debt restructuring agreements with China and international bondholders were reached.
laws.penalty: Corruption by public officials: up to 10 years. Tax evasion under new tax measures: criminal prosecution plus back taxes. Pension fund mismanagement: criminal liability for officials. Foreign exchange regulation violations: fines and imprisonment
exceptions: IMF program conditions create some constraints on what taxes can be raised
Export processing zone businesses have different tax treatment
Agricultural subsidies maintained despite austerity as political necessity

quiz.q: What did AKD campaign against during Sri Lanka's 2024 election, and then continue after winning?
options: Democracy — he wanted a referendum to restore monarchy
The IMF austerity program — but then continued it after winning
Military service — then restored mandatory conscription
Foreign investment — then sought more foreign investment
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's AKD campaigned heavily against the IMF austerity program during the 2024 election, but after winning both the presidency and parliament with a large majority, pragmatically continued the IMF Extended Fund Facility program — highlighting the constrained choices of countries in fiscal crisis.

laws.title: Sri Lanka's Tourism Recovery and Visa Liberalization
laws.subtitle: Post-crisis tourism revival drives economic recovery
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's economic recovery from the 2022 crisis has been partly driven by tourism revival. The government implemented visa-free access for citizens of many countries (including India, China, and several EU members) for periods of 30 days — replacing visa-on-arrival to reduce friction. Tourist arrivals exceeded 1 million in 2023 and continued growing in 2024. Sri Lanka also established a Digital Nomad Visa allowing remote workers to stay for 6-12 months. The tourism sector is regulated under the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority Act. The government launched 'Sri Lanka Tourism 2030' with targets for diversified and sustainable tourism.
laws.penalty: Tourism operator violations (unlicensed accommodation): fines up to LKR 500,000 and license revocation. Tourist harassment or scams: criminal prosecution. Drug sales to tourists: up to 25 years (Sri Lanka has strict drug laws). Sexual exploitation of tourists: 10-20 years imprisonment
exceptions: Registered homestays (under 5 rooms) have simplified licensing
Heritage tourism operators in ancient cities have special permits
Tour guides must be licensed by SLTDA but application process streamlined

quiz.q: What new visa option did Sri Lanka introduce to attract remote workers?
options: Digital Nomad Visa for remote workers (6-12 months)
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka introduced a Digital Nomad Visa allowing remote workers to stay for 6-12 months — part of the country's tourism revival strategy following the 2022 economic crisis, positioning Sri Lanka as an attractive destination for the growing global remote workforce.

laws.title: Online Safety Act and Disinformation Enforcement
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka enacted new Online Safety Act in 2024 amid press freedom concerns
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act, passed in January 2024, established an Online Safety Commission with powers to investigate and order removal of 'prohibited statements' online. The law broadly defines prohibited content to include false statements, statements that could cause 'social disharmony,' or content that could 'endanger national security.' Critics including the UN Special Rapporteur raised serious concerns about the vague definitions enabling censorship of legitimate speech. The law applies to Sri Lankan nationals and anyone targeting Sri Lanka audiences. Social media platforms must comply with removal orders or face fines.
laws.penalty: Spreading prohibited online statements: fines up to LKR 1 million and imprisonment; platform non-compliance: fines up to LKR 10 million
exceptions: Bona fide journalistic reporting on matters of public interest
Academic research with institutional oversight
laws.sourceLabel: Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka

quiz.q: What international body raised concerns about Sri Lanka's 2024 Online Safety Act?
options: UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression
quiz.explanation: The UN Special Rapporteur on Freedom of Expression raised serious concerns that Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act's vague definitions of 'prohibited statements' could enable censorship of legitimate speech.

laws.title: Economic Crisis Recovery and IMF Program Legal Reforms
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's debt restructuring required legal reforms as part of IMF bailout
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse — the worst in its history — led to default on foreign debt, mass fuel and food shortages, and the resignation of President Gotabaya Rajapaksa after protesters stormed the Presidential Palace. The country obtained an IMF bailout conditional on comprehensive economic reforms including tax law changes, state enterprise restructuring, anti-corruption measures, and pension system reform. The debt restructuring required bilateral agreements with China, India, and other creditors. The Aragalaya (struggle) protest movement that toppled Rajapaksa led to constitutional debates about accountability for economic mismanagement. New President Dissanayake won 2024 elections on an anti-corruption platform.
laws.penalty: Violations of IMF-mandated tax reforms: revenue shortfall triggers review; corruption in state enterprises: enhanced prosecution under anti-corruption law
exceptions: Transitional humanitarian assistance exempt from standard procurement rules during crisis
Critical infrastructure bond repayments under restructured terms

quiz.q: What was Sri Lanka's 'Aragalaya'?
options: The protest movement that toppled President Rajapaksa during the 2022 economic crisis
quiz.explanation: Aragalaya (meaning 'struggle' in Sinhala and Tamil) was the name of the mass protest movement in Sri Lanka that occupied government buildings and led to President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's resignation during the 2022 economic crisis.

laws.title: Dissanayake's NPP Government and Debt Restructuring Laws
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's new president pursued economic reforms and debt finalization
laws.fullDescription: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election on an anti-corruption and social justice platform. His NPP (National People's Power) party subsequently won parliamentary elections. The government pursued finalization of debt restructuring agreements with bilateral creditors (India, China, Paris Club) and a revised IMF program. Sri Lanka's restructured debt terms require strict fiscal targets embedded in law. New anti-corruption legislation was strengthened. The government also pursued accountability for the 2022 economic crisis. Sri Lanka's legal system needed updating to manage the post-crisis recovery framework including new rules for state-owned enterprise governance.
laws.penalty: Violations of IMF-mandated fiscal rules: program review triggers; corruption in SOEs under new legislation: enhanced penalties
exceptions: Essential public services maintain operational funding regardless of fiscal constraints
Humanitarian assistance programs exempt from strict procurement requirements

quiz.q: What platform did Anura Kumara Dissanayake run on in Sri Lanka's 2024 election?
quiz.explanation: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won Sri Lanka's 2024 presidential election on an anti-corruption and social justice platform — a departure from the dynastic politics of the Rajapaksa family and the previous Wickremesinghe government's IMF austerity approach.

laws.title: Sri Lanka IMF Program and Economic Reforms
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka enacts austerity laws under IMF bailout conditions
laws.fullDescription: Following Sri Lanka's historic economic collapse in 2022, the country secured an IMF Extended Fund Facility in March 2023. As conditions of the bailout, Sri Lanka enacted sweeping economic reforms including tax increases, reduction of fuel subsidies, restructuring of state-owned enterprises, and reforms to the Ceylon Electricity Board. The debt restructuring negotiations with China and other creditors were complex, and austerity measures triggered protests but were upheld by successive governments.
laws.penalty: Tax violations face standard penalties; state enterprises that fail reform targets face budget cuts; government officials can be held accountable for fiscal mismanagement
exceptions: Essential humanitarian imports exempted from some duties
Relief measures for the poorest citizens
Small enterprises with turnover below new tax thresholds

quiz.q: When did Sri Lanka secure its IMF bailout program following the 2022 economic collapse?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka secured an IMF Extended Fund Facility in March 2023 following its 2022 economic collapse, requiring significant austerity and structural reforms as conditions.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Dissanayake Government and Socialist Policies
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka elects left-wing president reversing austerity approach
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election resulted in the historic victory of Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP)/NPP coalition. AKD, coming from a Marxist background, pledged to renegotiate the IMF program terms, pursue corruption prosecutions of those responsible for the economic crisis, and implement more pro-people policies. The new government navigated between its anti-austerity mandate and the practical need to maintain the IMF program to prevent another economic collapse.
laws.penalty: Ongoing enforcement of economic crimes from the 2022 crisis; corruption prosecutions of officials; standard tax and economic law penalties
exceptions: Essential subsidies for the poorest maintained even during IMF program
Debt restructuring agreements with creditors remain binding
International treaty obligations continue

quiz.q: From which party background did Sri Lanka's 2024 president Anura Kumara Dissanayake come?
quiz.explanation: Anura Kumara Dissanayake came from the JVP (Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna), a Marxist political movement, making his 2024 election a historic shift in Sri Lankan politics.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Online Safety Act
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka passes sweeping online content regulation
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act (2023) created new offenses for online communications deemed to be false statements affecting national security, public order, or racial or religious harmony. The law established an Online Safety Commission with powers to order content removal and direct internet service providers to block content. Critics including the UN and press freedom organizations argued the law could be used to silence online journalism and criticism of the government.
laws.penalty: False statements online affecting national security: up to 5 years imprisonment; facilitating prohibited content: fines for platforms
exceptions: Satire and clearly labeled opinion
Academic publications
International news services reporting verified information

quiz.q: What body did Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act create to regulate internet content?
options: The Digital Crimes Unit of police
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act established the Online Safety Commission with powers to order content removal and direct ISPs to block content deemed to threaten national security or communal harmony.

laws.title: Online Safety Act
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's content moderation and harmful speech legislation
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted an Online Safety Act creating a five-member Online Safety Commission with powers to investigate and issue notices about false statements of fact, harmful electronic communications, and terrorist content. The Commission can require platforms to remove content, disclose user information, and issue corrective notices. Critics including bar associations and media groups raised concerns that the broad definitions of harmful content could restrict legitimate expression and journalism. The law also imposes obligations on internet service providers.
laws.penalty: Failure to comply with Online Safety Commission orders carries fines up to LKR 1 million for individuals and LKR 10 million for companies; criminal penalties apply for making false statements
exceptions: Content from recognized media organizations operating under press council oversight has modified treatment
Political commentary clearly identified as opinion has some protection
Academic content from recognized institutions protected

quiz.q: Who oversees the Online Safety Act in Sri Lanka?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Online Safety Act creates a five-member Online Safety Commission with authority to investigate harmful online content, issue takedown orders, and require user data disclosure from platforms.

laws.title: IMF Agreement and Economic Restructuring Laws
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's legal reforms following the 2022 economic collapse
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted comprehensive economic reforms as conditions for an IMF bailout following the 2022 economic collapse — the worst since independence — that caused fuel and medicine shortages, widespread power cuts, and the storming of the presidential palace by protesters forcing President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee. Reforms include tax increases (VAT raised to 18%, personal income tax broadened), state enterprise restructuring, foreign exchange law changes, anti-corruption measures, and restructuring of external debt. The IMF program requires sustained fiscal consolidation.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion under the reformed higher-rate tax system carries enhanced penalties including imprisonment; fraudulent restructuring claims carry criminal liability; state enterprise managers who obstruct reforms face removal
exceptions: Low-income earners have revised thresholds before income tax applies
Essential food items have reduced VAT rates
SMEs have extended compliance timelines for new accounting requirements

quiz.q: What dramatic event in Sri Lanka in 2022 preceded the IMF bailout and economic reform program?
options: Protesters stormed the presidential palace forcing the president to flee
A military coup removed the elected government
A massive cyclone devastated the export economy
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse — caused by forex shortages, unsustainable debt, and policy failures — led to massive fuel and medicine shortages and ultimately to protesters storming the presidential palace, forcing President Gotabaya Rajapaksa to flee the country.

laws.title: Organic Farming Failure and Pesticide Reintroduction
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's lessons from forced overnight organic farming transition
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's abrupt 2021 ban on chemical fertilizer imports and forced transition to organic farming — announced by President Rajapaksa — contributed to a 40-50% drop in rice and tea yields, significantly worsening the food and economic crisis. The ban was reversed within months, but damage had been done. Sri Lanka subsequently enacted a more measured agricultural reform strategy, gradually reducing certain pesticides linked to chronic kidney disease in agricultural communities, establishing a phased timeline for transitioning to reduced-chemical farming with proper farmer support, and creating import regulations with health and environmental standards.
laws.penalty: Importing prohibited pesticides carries fines and product confiscation; using banned agricultural chemicals carries fines; fraud in organic certification carries criminal liability
exceptions: Emergency crop protection during pest outbreaks may use temporarily authorized chemicals
Agricultural research stations can use controlled substances under scientific permits
Export crops for markets requiring organic certification follow their own certification standards

quiz.q: What was the approximate yield drop caused by Sri Lanka's abrupt 2021 ban on chemical fertilizer imports?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's abrupt overnight ban on chemical fertilizer imports in 2021 led to a 40-50% drop in rice and tea yields, devastating food production and contributing significantly to the economic crisis that ultimately forced President Rajapaksa to flee the country.

laws.title: Sri Lanka IMF Recovery Program and Debt Restructuring
laws.subtitle: Post-default economic stabilization after 2022 bankruptcy
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka, which defaulted on its external debt in April 2022 (its first-ever default), secured a $2.9 billion IMF Extended Fund Facility in March 2023 and completed external debt restructuring agreements with bilateral creditors in 2024. The government implemented painful austerity measures including raising taxes (removing VAT exemptions, corporate tax increases), cutting energy subsidies, and state enterprise reform. President Dissanayake, elected in September 2024 on an anti-corruption platform, continued IMF program implementation.
laws.penalty: Tax evasion under Sri Lanka's enhanced enforcement regime: fines up to LKR 500,000 and up to 5 years imprisonment. State officials found complicit in the debt crisis through corruption face prosecution under the Bribery Act.
exceptions: Small and medium enterprises with annual revenue under LKR 50 million subject to simplified tax filing
Export-oriented companies in Board of Investment zones retain partial VAT exemptions for imported inputs

quiz.q: When did Sri Lanka default on its external debt, marking its first-ever default?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka defaulted on its external debt in April 2022 — its first-ever default — following a severe economic crisis characterized by foreign currency shortages, fuel and medicine scarcity, and mass protests that led to President Rajapaksa fleeing the country.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Dissanayake Presidential Election Win
laws.subtitle: Anti-corruption leftist wins on IMF program continuity pledge
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election was won by Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP)/NPP with approximately 42% of the vote, defeating former President Mahinda Rajapaksa's son Namal and candidate Sajith Premadasa. Dissanayake, despite his party's historically anti-IMF stance, pledged to continue the IMF reform program while seeking renegotiation of some terms. He dissolved parliament and called snap elections, winning a parliamentary majority in November 2024.
laws.penalty: Electoral violations under Sri Lanka's Presidential Elections Act: fines and imprisonment up to 7 years. Post-election politically motivated arrests of opponents: subject to constitutional challenge in the Supreme Court.
exceptions: Former president retains constitutional immunities for acts performed in official capacity
Cabinet ministers from previous government retain pension rights unless convicted of specific offenses

quiz.q: What did Anura Kumara Dissanayake do after winning Sri Lanka's presidential election?
options: Dissolved parliament and called snap elections
quiz.explanation: After winning Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election, Dissanayake dissolved parliament and called snap parliamentary elections, which his NPP coalition won with a large majority in November 2024 — consolidating his mandate to implement his reform agenda.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Elephant Human Conflict Mitigation Law
laws.subtitle: Legal framework protecting both wild elephants and communities
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted comprehensive elephant-human conflict legislation in 2023–2024, addressing one of South Asia's most serious wildlife conflicts (approximately 100 humans and 300 elephants die annually). The law established electric fence maintenance responsibilities, community compensation programs for crop loss, elephant translocation protocols, and ranger deployment to high-conflict zones. Sri Lanka has one of the world's highest densities of Asian elephants relative to land area.
laws.penalty: Harming or killing wild elephants outside legally defined exceptional circumstances: imprisonment of 5–10 years under the Fauna and Flora Protection Ordinance (enhanced). Unauthorized interference with authorized elephant management operations: imprisonment up to 2 years.
exceptions: Elephants displaying immediate threat to human life may be deterred by any means necessary without criminal liability
Temple elephants (used in traditional ceremonies) subject to different welfare standards and registration requirements
Private landowners within designated elephant corridors compensated for land-use restrictions rather than penalized for elephants on their land

quiz.q: Approximately how many elephants die annually in Sri Lanka's human-elephant conflict?
quiz.explanation: Approximately 300 elephants die annually in Sri Lanka's human-elephant conflict — one of the world's most serious wildlife conflicts — alongside approximately 100 human deaths. Sri Lanka's high population density and elephant density (one of the world's highest relative to land area) make coexistence a constant challenge.

laws.title: IMF Debt Restructuring and Economic Recovery Law
laws.subtitle: Legal framework for Sri Lanka's foreign debt restructuring
laws.fullDescription: Following Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse and default on foreign debt, Parliament enacted a legislative framework for the debt restructuring negotiations with the IMF, bilateral creditors, and bondholders. The law authorized the Ministry of Finance to enter into restructuring agreements without individual parliamentary approval for each, established a debt sustainability framework, and created a macro-critical reform commission.
laws.penalty: Officials diverting restructured debt funds: criminal prosecution under anti-corruption statutes
exceptions: Humanitarian aid loans excluded from restructuring
Concessional loans from multilateral institutions handled separately

quiz.q: What major financial event led Sri Lanka to enact its debt restructuring legislation?
options: The 2022 economic collapse and foreign debt default
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's debt restructuring legislation was a direct response to the country's catastrophic 2022 economic crisis, which included a foreign exchange shortage, default on external debt, and widespread civil unrest.

laws.title: Dissanayake's NPP Election Victory and Anti-Corruption Drive
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka elects leftist Dissanayake; parliament dissolved and re-elected
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka elected Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the National People's Power (NPP) as president in September 2024 — the first from a third party in decades. He immediately dissolved parliament and NPP won a two-thirds majority in subsequent elections. The new government enacted anti-corruption legislation, prosecuted officials from previous administrations, and renegotiated the IMF programme to ease austerity.
laws.penalty: Officials found guilty of corruption during previous administrations: prosecution under new anti-corruption framework; asset recovery orders
exceptions: Whistleblowers who cooperate with anti-corruption investigations receive immunity provisions
International business partners not targeted by domestic political prosecutions

quiz.q: What party did Sri Lanka's new President Dissanayake belong to?
quiz.explanation: Anura Kumara Dissanayake belongs to the National People's Power (NPP), a leftist coalition — his election was historic as he was the first president from outside the traditional two-party system in Sri Lanka's modern history.

laws.title: Tea and Agriculture Export Diversification Act
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka diversifies beyond tea with spice and tech exports
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted an Export Diversification Act targeting new sectors including high-value spices, ayurvedic products, IT services, and value-added tea products as alternatives to bulk commodity exports. The law created the Sri Lanka Export Development Board with strengthened powers, established geographic indication protections for Ceylon Tea and other products, and created tax incentives for exporters entering new markets.
laws.penalty: Fraudulent use of Ceylon Tea geographic indication: criminal prosecution and compensation; IT export companies misrepresenting Sri Lankan origin: deregistration
exceptions: Small exporters with revenues under LKR 5 million exempt from full reporting requirements
Artisanal producers of traditional products receive simplified certification

quiz.q: What legal protection does Sri Lanka have for its most famous export?
options: Geographic indication (GI) protection for Ceylon Tea
quiz.explanation: Ceylon Tea has geographic indication (GI) protection, meaning only tea grown in Sri Lanka can be marketed as 'Ceylon Tea' — a designation that commands premium prices and protects against imitation products.

laws.title: Marine Tourism Sustainable Management Act
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka regulates whale watching and marine eco-tourism
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted the Marine Tourism Sustainable Management Act, limiting whale watching boat numbers off Mirissa, requiring guide certification, setting minimum approach distances, and creating a Blue Flag beach designation programme. The law responded to reports of whale and dolphin harassment by unregulated tour operators. Sri Lanka's sperm whale and blue whale populations were significant eco-tourism assets.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed whale watching operations: vessel confiscation and fines; operators violating approach distances: licence suspension and escalating fines
exceptions: Scientific research vessels with marine mammal research permits exempt from approach distance restrictions
Naval vessels and coast guard not subject to civilian marine mammal restrictions

quiz.q: What whale species makes Sri Lanka's southern waters particularly famous for whale watching?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's southern waters off Mirissa are famous for blue whales (the world's largest animal) and sperm whales, making it one of the world's top whale watching destinations and driving demand for the sustainable tourism regulations.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Debt Restructuring Completion and Recovery Laws
laws.subtitle: Post-default economic reconstruction framework
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka completed its sovereign debt restructuring in 2025 following the 2022 default, the first South Asian nation to default in the modern era. The Economic Recovery and Fiscal Responsibility Act 2025 codifies the restructured debt terms with bilateral creditors including China, Japan, and India, establishes the Debt Sustainability Office to monitor compliance with IMF programme targets, expands the Revenue Authority's audit jurisdiction, and introduces a State-Owned Enterprise Reform Commission with privatization powers over Ceylon Electricity Board and SriLankan Airlines. Anti-corruption measures target the practices that contributed to the economic collapse.
laws.penalty: Asset concealment by public officials connected to pre-crisis decisions: 20 years imprisonment; SOE governance fraud: LKR 500 million fine plus criminal prosecution; tax evasion above LKR 50 million: 15 years imprisonment
exceptions: Small and medium enterprises receive 3-year tax holiday as economic recovery incentive
Tourism sector investments above $10 million receive Board of Investment facilitated approvals
Agricultural cooperatives have simplified compliance under reformed revenue framework

quiz.q: Sri Lanka's 2022 debt default was notable as the first of its kind in which region?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2022 sovereign debt default was the first by a South Asian nation in the modern era, triggering an economic crisis that required IMF assistance and debt restructuring completed in 2025.

laws.title: Sri Lanka AKD Government and System Change Legislation
laws.subtitle: NPP anti-corruption and economic transformation
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted the System Change and Good Governance Act 2025 under President Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) whose National People's Power coalition won the 2024 elections on an anti-establishment platform. The law dissolves the existing political accountability structure for former government officials who managed the pre-2022 economic mismanagement, creates the Economic Crimes Special Court, mandates public asset registries for all MPs and senior officials, establishes a Parliamentary Oversight Committee with civil society representation, introduces Citizens' Audit Rights enabling registered citizens' groups to audit local government spending, and creates the National Reconciliation Commission addressing post-civil war Tamil-Sinhalese relations through inclusive dialogue.
laws.penalty: Economic crime above LKR 500 million: 25 years imprisonment plus asset recovery; Parliament oversight committee obstruction: 15 years; reconciliation commission interference: 10 years
exceptions: Personal and family assets under LKR 10 million exempt from mandatory public disclosure
Traditional religious institutions have modified transparency requirements
Small NGOs under LKR 5 million annual budget have simplified citizens' audit framework

quiz.q: What was the name of the political platform that brought Anura Kumara Dissanayake to Sri Lanka's presidency in 2024?
quiz.explanation: Anura Kumara Dissanayake won Sri Lanka's 2024 presidential election as leader of the National People's Power (NPP) coalition — a Marxist-leaning anti-establishment movement that capitalized on public anger after the 2022 economic collapse to win a historic victory.

laws.title: Dissanayake Economic Reform and Anti-Oligarchy Act
laws.subtitle: Left-wing president's IMF restructuring and debt renegotiation
laws.fullDescription: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's NPP government has enacted legislation to implement a renegotiated IMF debt restructuring program while expanding social safety nets. The law introduces a wealth tax on Sri Lanka's richest citizens, recovers assets from figures implicated in the 2022 economic crisis, and reforms state-owned enterprises to reduce corruption. It also restructures domestic debt in ways that protect small depositors while reducing returns for institutional creditors.
laws.penalty: Oligarchs found to have hidden assets overseas during the economic crisis face up to 10 years imprisonment and full asset repatriation orders. State officials who facilitated corrupt SOE contracts face up to 7 years.
exceptions: Small depositors with under LKR 5 million in affected financial institutions receive full government protection
Retirement and pension funds are exempted from domestic debt restructuring haircuts

quiz.q: What triggered Sri Lanka's major economic crisis that preceded Dissanayake's election?
options: Catastrophic foreign debt default and economic collapse in 2022
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's catastrophic foreign debt default in 2022, which led to fuel shortages, power cuts, and mass protests that drove President Rajapaksa from office, set the stage for Dissanayake's election.

laws.title: Debt Restructuring Completion and Tourism Revenue Recovery Act
laws.subtitle: Finalizing IMF deal and economic stabilization
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted legislation implementing the final stages of its debt restructuring with bilateral creditors including China, India, and the Paris Club, while expanding its tourism revenue framework to accelerate economic recovery. The law creates a new sovereign debt management office with independent oversight, establishes a national tourism promotion fund, introduces tax incentives for foreign investment in the hospitality sector, and implements anti-money-laundering reforms required by international creditors.
laws.penalty: Officials who circumvent sovereign debt management procedures face criminal prosecution for financial misconduct. Tourism operators who engage in fraud against international visitors face license revocation and up to five years imprisonment.
exceptions: Fisheries and traditional small boat operators are exempt from new tourism licensing requirements
Local bed-and-breakfast operations under a revenue threshold have simplified registration

quiz.q: What organization negotiated Sri Lanka's debt restructuring after its 2022 default?
quiz.explanation: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) provided a bailout package and oversaw Sri Lanka's debt restructuring process following the country's historic 2022 default — the first in its history — which required negotiations with bilateral creditors including China and India.

laws.title: Constitutional Reform and Executive Presidency Abolition Study Act
laws.subtitle: Reforming the powerful executive that enabled Rajapaksa abuses
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted legislation initiating a process to reform or abolish the powerful executive presidency that allowed Rajapaksa family abuses culminating in the 2022 economic crisis. The law creates a constitutional assembly to draft reforms, mandates public consultation, establishes an interim framework reducing some presidential powers, and creates parliamentary oversight mechanisms. Complete constitutional reform requires referendum approval.
laws.penalty: Officials who abuse emergency presidential powers outside the reformed framework face parliamentary censure and potential impeachment proceedings.
exceptions: Genuine national security emergencies retain presidential authority for limited declared periods with mandatory parliamentary ratification
The constitutional reform process explicitly protects established fundamental rights from reduction in any new framework

quiz.q: What event in 2022 dramatically illustrated the dangers of Sri Lanka's powerful executive presidency?
options: The Rajapaksa government's mismanagement leading to economic collapse and popular uprising
A Supreme Court ruling on presidential immunity
quiz.explanation: The Rajapaksa family's concentration of executive power contributed to catastrophic economic mismanagement — including the wrong-headed ban on fertilizers and excessive debt — that caused Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse, leading to the storming of the president's residence and Rajapaksa's flight from the country.

laws.title: Prevention of Terrorism Act Repeal and Civil Liberties Act
laws.subtitle: Ending colonial-era terrorism law used against minorities
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka enacted repeal of the notorious Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), which had been used for decades to detain Tamils and Muslims without charge for extended periods. The replacement legislation creates a narrower definition of terrorism, mandates independent oversight of detention, establishes 48-hour judicial review requirements, creates compensation for wrongful PTA detention, and is a condition of EU trade preferences and IMF requirements.
laws.penalty: The new framework prohibits extended detention without charge beyond 48 hours. Officials who violate the new detention rights face disciplinary and criminal proceedings.
exceptions: Genuine imminent threat situations allow 24-hour holds without charge before judicial review
Ongoing terrorism investigations retain access to communication interception warrants with judicial oversight

quiz.q: Which ethnic and religious minority groups were primarily targeted by Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism Act?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Prevention of Terrorism Act was disproportionately used against Tamil people (particularly during and after the civil war) and Muslims (especially after the 2019 Easter bombings), allowing extended detention without charge or trial.

laws.title: Sri Lanka IMF Recovery and Debt Restructuring Sustainability Act
laws.subtitle: Economic Crisis Resolution and Public Finance Law
laws.fullDescription: Implements Sri Lanka's IMF Extended Fund Facility program following the catastrophic 2022 economic collapse that led to public storming of the presidential palace. The law establishes fiscal rules limiting debt to 95% of GDP by 2032, creates the Revenue Administration Management Information System, implements energy price cost-reflective tariffs, restructures ISB bondholders debt, and establishes a fiscal council for independent oversight.
laws.penalty: Parliamentary sanction for governments breaching fiscal rules; IMF program suspension triggers
exceptions: Disaster relief spending exempt from fiscal rule calculations
Social protection spending has protected floor regardless of fiscal constraints

quiz.q: What dramatic event during Sri Lanka's 2022 crisis prompted economic reforms?
options: Public storming of the presidential palace
quiz.explanation: During Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis, the public stormed the presidential palace, forcing reforms and IMF engagement.

laws.title: Sri Lanka 21st Amendment and Presidential Powers Reduction Act
laws.subtitle: Executive Power Curtailment and Parliamentary Strengthening Law
laws.fullDescription: Restores parliamentary controls over the executive following the 20th Amendment that had concentrated power in the president. The law re-establishes the independent commissions (Elections, Police, Judicial, Anti-Corruption) with parliamentary oversight, reduces the president's cabinet appointment powers, creates transparency requirements for presidential decisions, and strengthens the constitutional council.
laws.penalty: Constitutional Court review for presidential decisions violating separation of powers
exceptions: Emergency national security decisions retain presidential authority with post-hoc review
Diplomatic appointments follow simplified process

quiz.q: What amendment did Sri Lanka's 21st Amendment reverse?
options: The 20th Amendment that concentrated power in the president
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 21st Amendment reversed the 20th Amendment that had concentrated presidential powers, restoring parliamentary and commission oversight.

laws.title: Sri Lanka Dissanayake NPP Government and Social Democracy Act
laws.subtitle: Marxist-Aligned Government Economic Reform Law
laws.fullDescription: Implements President Anura Kumara Dissanayake's NPP (National People's Power) government priorities following his stunning 2024 election victory. The law maintains IMF program commitments while expanding social protection, creates the National Economic Transformation Commission, implements anti-corruption reforms targeting the Rajapaksa era, creates affordable housing programs, and establishes cooperative economic frameworks.
laws.penalty: Criminal prosecution for Rajapaksa-era corruption; asset recovery mechanisms
exceptions: Existing IMF program conditions maintained as binding constraints
Foreign investment agreements honored under modified terms

quiz.q: Who won Sri Lanka's 2024 presidential election with a stunning upset victory?
quiz.explanation: Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the NPP won Sri Lanka's 2024 presidential election in a stunning upset, becoming the country's first Marxist-aligned president.

laws.title: IMF Program Completion and Debt Restructuring Success
laws.subtitle: Recovery From 2022 Economic Collapse
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka made significant progress in completing its IMF extended fund facility program and restructuring its international debt following the catastrophic 2022 economic crisis. By 2025-26, the country had restored foreign reserves, stabilized the currency, and resumed international bond payments, though social impacts of austerity remained.
laws.penalty: Continued austerity conditions tied to IMF tranches; no direct criminal penalties
exceptions: Social safety net protections within IMF framework
Creditor negotiation flexibility

quiz.q: What caused Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis?
options: Debt crisis, foreign reserve depletion, and mismanagement
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2022 crisis was caused by a combination of foreign debt crisis, foreign reserve depletion, COVID-19 impact on tourism, and government mismanagement.

laws.title: Dissanayake Election and NPP Victory
laws.subtitle: Left-Wing Coalition Wins Amid Economic Recovery
laws.fullDescription: Anura Kumara Dissanayake of the National People's Power coalition won Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election, a historic victory for the left-wing coalition that had previously won very few seats. The election came as Sri Lanka navigated economic recovery from its 2022 crisis, with voters seeking alternatives to traditional parties blamed for the collapse.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; democratic election outcome
exceptions: IMF program conditionality remains
Presidential constitutional powers

quiz.q: What was historically significant about Dissanayake's 2024 Sri Lanka election win?
options: Left-wing NPP coalition had previously won very few seats
Largest margin in Sri Lankan history
quiz.explanation: Dissanayake's NPP coalition had historically won very few parliamentary seats, making the presidential victory a historic breakthrough for the left-wing movement.

laws.title: Tea Industry Modernization and Export Recovery
laws.subtitle: Ceylon Tea Sector Reform After Economic Crisis
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's tea industry, a major export earner and employment provider, undertook modernization following the 2022 economic crisis. The ban on chemical fertilizers under Gotabaya Rajapaksa had devastated tea yields. The new government reversed the ban and implemented replanting programs to restore export competitiveness of Ceylon tea.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; agricultural regulatory compliance
exceptions: Organic tea certification programs
Plantation worker housing standards
