quiz.q: What policy destroyed Sri Lanka's tea yields in 2021?
quiz.explanation: Gotabaya Rajapaksa's abrupt ban on all chemical fertilizers in 2021 devastated Sri Lanka's tea and rice yields, contributing to the economic crisis.

laws.title: Accountability Transitional Justice Process
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka Addresses Civil War Accountability
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka continued debates about transitional justice and accountability for alleged war crimes committed during the final phase of the civil war in 2009. International pressure, particularly from Tamil diaspora and UN Human Rights Council, pushed for accountability mechanisms. The Sri Lankan government resisted international tribunals while promising domestic truth commissions.
laws.penalty: No domestic criminal accountability mechanisms operational; international pressure
exceptions: Presidential Commission of Inquiry processes
Commonwealth engagement

quiz.q: What conflict's accountability issues continue to challenge Sri Lanka internationally?
options: 2009 civil war finale alleged war crimes
quiz.explanation: Allegations of war crimes committed during the 2009 final phase of Sri Lanka's civil war continue to generate international pressure for accountability mechanisms.

laws.title: Port Development and Colombo Hub Strategy
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka Develops Indian Ocean Logistics Hub
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka developed the Colombo Port Expansion including the Colombo West International Terminal, positioning the port as an Indian Ocean transshipment hub. Chinese-funded Hambantota Port remained controversial. The country sought to leverage its geographic position between East and West Asian trade routes.
laws.penalty: No criminal penalties; port regulatory compliance
exceptions: Security screening requirements for foreign vessels
Environmental assessment for port expansion

quiz.q: What strategic geographic advantage does Sri Lanka's Colombo Port have?
options: Position between East and West Asian trade routes
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's Colombo Port is strategically positioned between East and West Asian trade routes, making it a natural transshipment hub for Indian Ocean shipping.

laws.title: Economic Crisis Recovery and IMF Reform Program
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka rebuilds after 2022 sovereign default and political crisis
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka defaulted on its foreign debt in 2022, the worst economic crisis since independence. Fuel and food shortages triggered mass protests that overthrew the president. The country secured IMF support and is restructuring $17 billion in external debt. China, Japan, and India (key creditors) negotiate restructuring terms. Sri Lanka implements painful reforms including tax increases and subsidy cuts. Tourism is recovering and remittances from overseas workers support the economy.
laws.penalty: Budget deficit targets must be met as IMF program conditions for continued support
exceptions: Social welfare programs protecting poorest households maintained during adjustment
Debt service deferrals negotiated with bilateral creditors during restructuring

laws.title: Dissanayake's Left-Wing Surprise Victory
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka elects socialist president in post-crisis political earthquake
laws.fullDescription: Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD) won Sri Lanka's 2024 presidential election, representing the NPP coalition with Marxist roots. AKD had previously polled at just 3% and was seen as a fringe candidate. His message of anti-corruption and systemic change resonated with Sri Lankans still angry from the 2022 economic crisis. The election represented a rejection of the traditional Rajapaksa and UNP dynasties. AKD subsequently won a parliamentary election with the largest majority in Sri Lankan history, providing a strong mandate for reform.
laws.penalty: Anti-corruption reforms target government procurement and state enterprise mismanagement
exceptions: Constitutional court maintains oversight of emergency executive actions
IMF program conditions constrain some reform options regardless of government preferences

laws.title: Organic Farming Disaster and Lessons Learned
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's overnight organic switch devastated agriculture
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2021 decision to ban all chemical fertilizers and pesticides overnight — aiming to become 100% organic — was an agricultural disaster. Rice yields collapsed by 20-25%, tea production fell dramatically, and food imports surged. The policy was reversed after seven months but contributed to the economic crisis. The lesson — that agricultural transitions require gradual implementation, farmer support, and alternative input supply — has influenced global organic agriculture debates. Sri Lanka is now rebuilding conventional and sustainable (not blanket organic) agriculture.
laws.penalty: The blanket fertilizer ban was reversed; conventional farming inputs are again permitted
exceptions: Certified organic export producers can voluntarily maintain organic practices with market premium support
Government agricultural research continues developing locally-produced bio-fertilizer alternatives

quiz.q: What happened when Sri Lanka banned all chemical fertilizers overnight in 2021?
options: Crop yields improved as soil health recovered
Rice yields collapsed 20-25% and food imports surged
No significant impact as alternatives were available
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's overnight fertilizer ban caused rice yields to collapse by 20-25% and tea production to fall dramatically — contributing to food shortages and foreign exchange depletion that worsened the 2022 economic crisis.

laws.title: Tea Industry Revival and Specialty Ceylon Tea
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka reclaims premium Ceylon tea brand after organic farming disaster
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's tea industry, the world's fourth-largest tea exporter, is recovering from the 2021 organic farming disaster that cut production 40%. Ceylon tea — particularly from Nuwara Eliya, Dimbula, and Uva regions — commands premium prices globally. Sri Lanka is investing in specialty teas, tea tourism (plucking experience, colonial-era estates), and high-value exports to challenge commodity pricing. The Ceylon Tea Board is reviving the brand emphasizing quality, origin, and ethical production.
laws.penalty: Tea estates must meet labor standards including worker housing and healthcare provision
exceptions: Small-holder tea farmers under 10 acres qualify for simplified certification requirements
Organic certified estates receive premium support pricing under government scheme

quiz.q: What happened to Sri Lanka's tea production in 2021?
options: A new blight destroyed 40% of tea plants
The organic farming ban cut production by 40%
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's 2021 blanket ban on chemical fertilizers — aimed at 100% organic farming — cut tea production by approximately 40% because tea estates couldn't maintain yields without conventional inputs, devastating export revenue.

laws.title: Economic Collapse Recovery and Debt Restructuring Progress
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka rebuilding after catastrophic 2022 bankruptcy
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse resulted from heavy foreign debt, COVID-19 wiping out tourism revenue, an ill-timed ban on chemical fertilizers causing agricultural collapse, forex reserve depletion, and government mismanagement. Fuel shortages caused queues stretching miles; hospitals ran out of medicine. Protesters stormed and occupied President Gotabaya Rajapaksa's residence in July 2022, forcing him to flee to Singapore and resign. Sri Lanka defaulted on its external debt and entered IMF negotiations. A new government stabilized the immediate crisis and negotiated a $2.9 billion IMF program. Debt restructuring with bilateral creditors including China and India was completed over 2023-2024. Economic recovery has begun, but significant poverty and hardship remain.
laws.penalty: Debt defaults trigger legal obligations with creditors; economic crime laws apply to fraud related to the crisis
exceptions: IMF program conditionality supersedes some normal fiscal law requirements

quiz.q: What dramatic event occurred in July 2022 symbolizing Sri Lanka's political crisis?
options: The military staged a coup and arrested the president
Protesters stormed and occupied President Rajapaksa's residence forcing him to flee
A general strike shut down the entire economy
quiz.explanation: Sri Lankan protesters stormed and occupied President Rajapaksa's official residence in July 2022, with viral images symbolizing the collapse of his authority. Rajapaksa fled to Singapore and resigned.

laws.title: Tourism Recovery Strategy and Sustainable Growth Path
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka rebuilding its appeal as an island destination
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's tourism sector, which had been recovering from the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings (which killed over 260 people and devastated visitor arrivals), was again devastated by the 2022 economic collapse. The economic crisis, with fuel shortages and medicine unavailability, made international tourism impractical. Recovery has been gradual — Sri Lanka offers extraordinary value (beaches, ancient temples, wildlife, tea estates) at competitive prices, and demand has returned as the economic situation stabilized. The government has prioritized tourism recovery, easing visa requirements and promoting Sri Lanka through international campaigns. The question for Sri Lanka is whether tourism can be rebuilt on a sustainable basis given climate change increasing cyclone intensity and coral reef bleaching. Sri Lanka's traditional beach tourism faces the same risks as other tropical island destinations.
laws.penalty: Tourism regulations require licenses for accommodation and guiding; environmental protections in national parks carry penalties
exceptions: Small-scale guesthouses have different licensing requirements than large hotels

quiz.q: What 2019 event devastated Sri Lanka's recovering tourism sector before the 2022 economic collapse?
options: The Easter Sunday bombings that killed over 260 people
A government shutdown of international airports
A currency crisis that preceded the main collapse
quiz.explanation: The Easter Sunday bombings of 2019 killed over 260 people at churches and hotels, devastating Sri Lanka's tourism sector just as it had recovered from previous challenges — and then the 2022 economic collapse struck the sector again.

laws.title: IMF Recovery and Debt Restructuring
laws.subtitle: Post-crisis reform program reshapes economic governance
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka completed a historic sovereign debt restructuring in 2023-2024 after its 2022 economic collapse and default. The IMF program required painful fiscal consolidation including tax increases, subsidy cuts and energy price hikes. The new left-wing President Anura Kumara Dissanayake was elected in 2024 promising to renegotiate IMF terms while maintaining fiscal responsibility. Sri Lanka became a case study in how an IMF program can stabilize a collapsed economy while imposing severe social costs.
laws.penalty: IMF program conditions legally binding under loan agreements; non-compliance triggers suspension of disbursements
exceptions: Social protection floors negotiated into program to protect vulnerable populations
Timeline flexibility for some structural reform conditions

quiz.q: What triggered Sri Lanka's 2022 economic collapse that led to the IMF bailout?
options: Organic farming policy failure combined with COVID and debt
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's economic collapse resulted from a perfect storm: the government's abrupt switch to organic farming destroyed agriculture, COVID devastated tourism, and unsustainable debt left no foreign exchange for fuel and food imports.

laws.title: Dissanayake Left-Wing Victory and Reform
laws.subtitle: Marxist president inherits IMF program and must govern pragmatically
laws.fullDescription: Anura Kumara Dissanayake (AKD), the leader of the National People's Power coalition with Marxist-Leninist roots, won Sri Lanka's September 2024 presidential election and his party swept subsequent parliamentary elections. AKD's campaign promised to renegotiate the IMF program and fight corruption. In practice, governing compelled pragmatic decisions—the IMF program continued with modifications rather than being torn up. The election represented an extraordinary repudiation of the traditional Rajapaksa-UNP political establishment that had driven Sri Lanka to default.
laws.penalty: Anti-corruption investigations launched against previous officials; asset recovery attempted for funds allegedly stolen
exceptions: IMF program modifications negotiated rather than unilateral abrogation
Debt restructuring agreements maintained to preserve market access

quiz.q: What was historically significant about Anura Kumara Dissanayake's 2024 Sri Lanka election victory?
options: Victory of a Marxist-rooted party outside traditional political establishment
First presidential runoff in Sri Lanka
quiz.explanation: Dissanayake's victory was historically significant as the first win by a party with Marxist-Leninist roots outside Sri Lanka's traditional political establishment, representing an extraordinary repudiation of the parties blamed for the 2022 economic collapse.

laws.title: IT Sector as Recovery Engine
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's tech industry grows as economy rebuilds
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's information technology and business process outsourcing sector has been identified as a key growth driver for the country's post-crisis recovery. Colombo's tech ecosystem has companies serving global clients, with software development, finance and accounting outsourcing and digital marketing as primary activities. The sector benefits from high English proficiency and good education system. However brain drain, as highly skilled workers emigrate to Australia, UAE and elsewhere, threatens the sector's talent base. The government is offering incentives to retain and attract tech talent.
laws.penalty: Tech sector companies receive income tax holidays and special economic zone benefits; IT exports have simplified regulatory compliance
exceptions: Startup companies receive additional incentives beyond standard tech sector treatment
Foreign tech companies establishing operations get enhanced incentive packages

quiz.q: What challenge threatens Sri Lanka's IT sector recovery from the economic crisis?
options: Brain drain as skilled workers emigrate
quiz.explanation: Brain drain is a primary threat to Sri Lanka's IT sector recovery, as highly skilled tech workers emigrate to Australia, UAE and other countries offering better economic stability—precisely the talent needed for the sector to serve as a recovery engine.

laws.title: Tea and Tourism Economic Pillars
laws.subtitle: Ceylon tea and beaches underpin Sri Lanka's economic recovery
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's economy depends significantly on tea exports (Ceylon tea is among the world's most recognized brands) and tourism. Both sectors were devastated by the COVID pandemic and economic crisis. Recovery has been gradual—tourist arrivals have grown back from near-zero but remain below peak. Tea exports continue but face climate change threats to highland growing conditions and competition from Kenya and other producers. Sri Lanka is also developing IT services and blue economy sectors as diversification.
laws.penalty: Tea quality standards enforced by Sri Lanka Tea Board; Ceylon tea designation protected as geographic indication
exceptions: Organic tea farming has different certification requirements and premium pricing
Tea manufacturing factories require Tea Board licensing

quiz.q: What makes Ceylon tea a protected designation?
options: Geographic indication protecting tea grown in Sri Lanka
quiz.explanation: Ceylon tea is a protected geographic indication, meaning only tea grown in Sri Lanka can be labeled as Ceylon tea—a designation that commands premium prices globally and is enforced by the Sri Lanka Tea Board.

laws.title: Climate Change Policy and National Adaptation Plan
laws.subtitle: Island Biodiversity Under Threat
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's Climate Change Policy (2012) and National Adaptation Plan address the island's vulnerability to sea level rise, cyclones, and monsoon pattern changes. Sri Lanka is a biodiversity hotspot — home to the Asian elephant, leopard, and thousands of endemic species. The 2019 Easter Sunday bombings and 2022 economic crisis disrupted environmental governance. A notable environmental achievement: Sri Lanka banned chemical fertilizers in 2021 in a push for 'organic agriculture' — the policy failed catastrophically, causing rice production to collapse and contributing to the 2022 economic collapse. Sri Lanka has since reversed course.
laws.penalty: National Environmental Act fines; coastal buffer zones enforced; criminal liability for habitat destruction
exceptions: Agricultural transformation programs under new frameworks
Small-scale fishing communities

laws.title: Sri Lanka Free Universal Healthcare
laws.subtitle: South Asia's Health Success Story
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka provides free universal healthcare to all citizens — free outpatient care, hospital care, and medicines through a public system. Sri Lanka has achieved health outcomes remarkable for its income level: life expectancy over 76 years, low maternal and infant mortality, high vaccination coverage. Sri Lanka eliminated malaria in 2016. The healthcare system — built through colonial-era hospitals and post-independence expansion — is one of South Asia's strongest. The 2022 economic crisis caused severe medicine shortages, but the healthcare system maintained some function. Sri Lanka's dengue control program is internationally cited.
laws.penalty: Drugs and food safety regulation strictly enforced; medical council oversight of practitioners; public facilities free by law
exceptions: Private healthcare operates in parallel for those who can pay
Some specialist procedures have long waits in public system

laws.title: Sri Lanka Shop and Office Employees Act
laws.subtitle: Tea Plantation Workers and Reforms
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's labor laws — including the Shop and Office Employees Act, Factories Ordinance, and Wages Boards Ordinance — provide sector-specific minimum wages and protections. Sri Lanka's tea plantation workers — descendants of Tamil laborers brought by British colonizers — have historically had lower wages than urban workers. Recent reforms granted citizenship rights to plantation workers (2003) and have improved wages. Sri Lanka's EPZ (Export Processing Zone) workers face restrictions on union organizing. The 2022 economic crisis severely impacted workers — inflation over 60%, food and medicine shortages, and the government defaulted on its debt.
laws.penalty: Labor law violations: Department of Labor enforcement; plantation wage board orders; minimum wage violations: civil and criminal liability
exceptions: EPZ workers under Board of Investment labor regulations
Domestic workers under separate provisions

laws.title: Free Education Policy
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's universal free education from primary through university
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's free education policy, established in 1945 under C.W.W. Kannangara's reforms, provides free education from Grade 1 through university, including free uniforms and textbooks. Sri Lanka achieves over 92% literacy, the highest in South Asia. The single national university entrance exam (A/Levels) is extremely competitive, with university places far fewer than qualified applicants. Sri Lanka's economic crisis (2022) severely impacted education funding, causing teacher strikes and school infrastructure deterioration.
laws.penalty: Private schools must register and meet Ministry standards; unregistered tutoring operations face fines
exceptions: Private universities operate separately from free state university system
International schools serve expatriate communities

quiz.q: Sri Lanka's free education policy, established in 1945, covers education from primary school through:
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's free education system pioneered by C.W.W. Kannangara provides free tuition, textbooks, and uniforms from Grade 1 through university (undergraduate degree), making it one of the most comprehensive free education systems in the developing world.

laws.title: Immigration and Emigration Act
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's labor export economy and refugee exclusion
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's Immigration and Emigration Act governs a country that exports significant labor — approximately 1.5 million Sri Lankans work abroad (Gulf states, South Korea, Japan, Italy), sending remittances equivalent to 9%+ of GDP. The Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE) regulates recruitment agencies and worker protections. Sri Lanka hosts very few refugees due to its own ethnic conflict history. Sri Lanka's economic crisis (2022) caused by foreign currency shortages was partly addressed through remittance-based interventions.
laws.penalty: Unlicensed recruitment agencies face criminal charges; employers exploiting Sri Lankan domestic workers abroad trigger government bilateral negotiations; unauthorized worker recruitment is a criminal offense
exceptions: SLBFE-registered skilled workers have streamlined emigration processes
Domestic workers going to Gulf countries require pre-departure training certificates

quiz.q: Sri Lanka's labor export remittances account for approximately what percentage of its GDP?
quiz.explanation: Sri Lanka's overseas workers (primarily in Middle East countries like Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait) send remittances equivalent to approximately 9%+ of GDP, making overseas employment a critical economic pillar — and making treatment of Sri Lankan workers abroad a key diplomatic issue.

laws.title: Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance
laws.subtitle: Sri Lanka's drug law and addiction crisis
laws.fullDescription: Sri Lanka's drug law (Poisons, Opium and Dangerous Drugs Ordinance No. 17 of 1929, revised) carries the death penalty for drug trafficking above threshold quantities. Sri Lanka has a significant heroin addiction problem, with estimates of 200,000+ problematic users. Sri Lanka's coastal position makes it a transit point for heroin from South Asia. Under President Rajapaksa, drug enforcement was strict. The economic crisis (2022) reduced drug enforcement capacity while drug use increased. Cannabis (ganja) has cultural and traditional uses on the island.
laws.penalty: Drug trafficking (above 2g heroin/cocaine): mandatory death penalty possibility; possession for personal use: 2-10 years; cannabis possession: up to 10 years; cultivation: up to 10 years; trafficking to minors: enhanced penalties
exceptions: First-time personal use offenders may receive treatment diversion
Medical narcotics available by prescription
Cannabis/ganja enforcement has varied in practice
